entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Samuel Bell (1770–1850) was an American Democratic-Republican and National Republican politician from New Hampshire who served as Governor of New Hampshire (1819–1823) and U.S. Senator (1823–1835). His combined executive and legislative career spanned the Era of Good Feelings through the early Jacksonian period — the transformation from the one-party fusion politics of Monroe's era to the sharp partisan divisions of Jackson's. New Hampshire in this period was transitioning from Federalist competition to Democratic dominance, making Bell's National Republican/anti-Jackson alignment increasingly difficult.

His Senate years covered the nullification crisis, the Bank War, and the emergence of the Whig Party from the anti-Jackson coalition — the central political conflicts of the 1820s and early 1830s.

He was a Chester New Hampshire lawyer who served in multiple capacities over more than a decade of public service.

He was among New Hampshire's most experienced antebellum politicians.
